headline: High: Mentat’s broad filesystem/network defaults can conflict with godot_rl_agents’ simulation context, creating leakage and cascading-error risk if outputs are reused without verification.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared channel is documented, so direct prompt injection is not default. However, Mentat reads/writes files and uses stdin/stdout, while godot_rl_agents is a codebase that could be manually bridged through files. That makes a manual copy-paste or file-based injection path plausible, but not strong.
conditions: IF an operator copies Mentat output into files that godot_rl_agents later consumes as instructions, injection becomes possible.
IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace without content provenance checks, file-based instruction smuggling is possible.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate directories.
Do not paste model output into executable or config files.
Add a human review step before any file is reused as instructions.
Use read-only mounts for any shared artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Mentat has broad network egress and reads selected files by default, while godot_rl_agents is an open-source code project with no isolation or data-handling controls shown. If sensitive code or secrets are placed in the shared workspace, Mentat can transmit file contents to its model provider. The pair therefore has a default leakage path through the filesystem and outbound API calls.
conditions: IF sensitive files are present in the directory Mentat is pointed at, those contents can be sent to the model provider.
IF the two agents share a workspace containing secrets or private source, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Exclude secrets and private repos from Mentat’s working tree.
Use a dedicated non-sensitive workspace for both agents.
Rotate any exposed API keys immediately after testing.
Restrict outbound network access during evaluation.
requires-engineering: add workspace-level access controls or sandboxing.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Mentat can write the filesystem and modify git state, and its shared-state model is via filesystem. godot_rl_agents is a code repository context, so concurrent edits can collide if both touch the same tree. No locking or coordination primitive is documented, so write conflicts are plausible in default multi-instance use.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git checkout, concurrent edits can overwrite each other.
IF Mentat is used while another process edits the same files, merge conflicts or lost updates can occur.
mitigations: Run only one writer per repository at a time.
Use separate branches for each agent.
Commit or stash before switching agents.
Review diffs before applying them.
requires-engineering: add file locks or orchestrator-level coordination.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Mentat produces diff-based edit proposals and can act on selected files, while godot_rl_agents is a codebase context that may be treated as authoritative input for edits. Without a documented verification layer between them, incorrect assumptions from one agent can propagate into the other’s proposed changes and then into the repository.
conditions: IF Mentat is asked to implement changes based on godot_rl_agents-generated text, errors can cascade into code edits.
IF the operator applies diffs without review, mistaken outputs can become committed changes.
mitigations: Require human review of every diff.
Ask Mentat to cite file paths and line numbers.
Cross-check outputs against source files before applying.
Keep tasks narrowly scoped to one change at a time.
requires-engineering: add automated validation/tests before commit.

E_compliance.rationale: No specific regulated data class, residency mismatch, or retention policy is documented for godot_rl_agents or Mentat. The only concrete compliance-relevant detail is Mentat’s handling of model provider API keys and outbound API calls, which can matter if regulated data is introduced, but that is not shown here. The other agent has no compliance surface documented.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Mentat’s workspace, outbound API processing may create a compliance issue.
IF the deployment requires residency or retention guarantees, no such controls are documented here.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in the workspace.
Confirm provider terms and retention settings before use.
Use synthetic or redacted inputs for testing.
Log what data classes are processed.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention.
